words.gloss: a bull (metaphor for a majestic leader)

literal: Army, subjects, wealth, ministry, allies, fortress—all these six, he who possesses, among kings, is a bull.
translation: He who possesses these six elements—an army, subjects, wealth, ministers, allies, and fortresses—is a bull among kings.
modern: படை, குடிமக்கள், செல்வம், அமைச்சர், நட்பு நாடுகள், அரண் ஆகிய ஆறு அங்கங்களையும் உடையவன் அரசர்களுள் ஆண் சிங்கம் போன்றவன் ஆவான்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the six essential components of a well-governed state. A ruler must have a strong army, loyal subjects, abundant resources, wise ministers, reliable allies, and secure fortifications. The word 'kūḻ' literally refers to food or grain, but in this context of statecraft, it represents the treasury and resources of the land. The poet uses the metaphor of 'ēṟu' (a strong bull or male beast) to describe a ruler who possesses all six elements as a majestic leader among peers.
